description: Risk-oriented behavioral scenarios and human-review rubrics; not agent-execution results

cases.scenario: Solution-first request with unsupported implementation choice
cases.input: Stakeholder: Build a new dashboard immediately. The underlying problem and success criteria were not supplied.

checks.criterion: Elicitor investigates the underlying need and success signal before accepting the dashboard as a requirement.
Does not convert the requested dashboard into an approved requirement or architecture without evidence.

cases.scenario: Dependent decisions about the end of a billing retry window
cases.input: Define a retry policy for a subscription. The grace-window origin is undecided; the last allowed instant and time zone depend on that choice. No owner has approved any of these decisions.

checks.criterion: Identifies the unresolved start of the window as a prerequisite to precise retry timing.
Does not silently decide the deadline, time zone, or late-arriving charge outcome.
Requests the next material decision rather than an unrelated exhaustive questionnaire.

cases.scenario: Known evidence should not be requested again
cases.input: Source S1 (authorized product policy): refund limit is 2 per user per rolling 365 days. The only unknown is whether pending refunds count toward the limit.

checks.criterion: Identifies the pending-refund treatment as unresolved and relevant to the rule.
Does not ask the user to restate the limit or time window already established by S1.

cases.scenario: Adjacent discovery must not silently expand the Change Boundary
cases.input: Approved change: expose a read-only refund count. During discovery a stakeholder suggests redesigning all refund processing; no scope authority approved the expansion.

checks.criterion: Preserves the approved read-only boundary and identifies the redesign as a separate proposal requiring authorization.
Does not include refund-process redesign in the current approved change or work items.

cases.scenario: Non-functional requirement lacks measurable fit criterion
cases.input: System shall be fast under load. No workload, performance metric, acceptable limit or verification environment has been authorized.

checks.criterion: Identifies missing workload/context, measure, justified threshold, and verification method for objective acceptance.
Does not fabricate a latency number, percentile, or workload to make the requirement appear testable.

cases.scenario: Temporal boundary is ambiguous
cases.input: A renewal attempt is permitted during grace period; the business did not define whether an attempt exactly at the grace-end timestamp is permitted or how in-flight attempts behave.

checks.criterion: Makes temporal trigger, inclusive/exclusive boundary, and in-flight behavior explicit as unresolved semantic concerns.
Does not claim the temporal property is formally verified or realized by an unspecified implementation.

cases.scenario: Scenario set needs counterexamples and identity preservation
cases.input: Requirement R1: only the owner can change an address. Existing scenario SC-7 covers an owner update. Need to evaluate a non-owner request and a concurrent owner update. No test framework specified.

checks.criterion: Preserves SC-7 identity while exploring relevant authorization counterexample and concurrency conditions.
Does not turn scenario identity into test filenames or generate executable tests without authorization.

cases.scenario: Contradictory authoritative policy sources
cases.input: Policy P1 says refunds are permitted within 7 days. Policy P2, from a different authority, says 14 days. There is no supersession decision. Spec R1 says 7 days.

checks.criterion: Reports a material conflict with source references and the missing authority decision.
Does not silently choose the newest or preferred policy and label the specification sufficient.
Does not edit the requirement during read-only validation.

cases.scenario: Safe vertical slicing of payment changes
cases.input: Authorized change: retry failed card charges with deduplication guarantee. Proposed slice A activates retries but postpones idempotency until slice B. Finance impact is material.

checks.criterion: Flags the initial slice as unsafe because it omits a required deduplication guarantee.
Does not split a critical guarantee across an unsafe intermediate release or invent design choices.

cases.scenario: End-to-end Requirements planning handoff with explicit, authorized refund-count semantics
cases.input: Authorized product decision S1 for a read-only refund count endpoint: GET /invoice/user/:userId/refunds/count?days=365. An authenticated user may request only their own userId; requests for another user are forbidden. userId is a required integer identifier; days is an optional positive integer with default 365. The response is the integer number of distinct invoices belonging to userId with StatusId=7 (REFUNDED), RefundedDate in the UTC rolling interval [nowUTC - days * 24 hours, nowUTC), and a valid RefundedDate; an invoice refunded partially still counts once. Invoices with StatusId=9 (REFUND_REQUESTED), missing RefundedDate, or outside the interval are excluded. When no invoices match, return count 0. S1 approves these semantics and the read-only scope. No database schema, SQL strategy, coding tasks, test framework, or rollout plan has been authorized. Request a validated requirements specification, traceable behavioral scenarios, and work items at the planning granularity justified by S1; do not invent technical implementation.

checks.criterion: Applies the authorized S1 semantics, routes the required Requirements capabilities, and states the actual validation/readiness outcome without claiming implementation or acceptance.
Produces coherent backlog items linked to the known authorized requirement and appropriate behavior scenarios, at granularity justified by S1; explicit non-blocking unknowns remain visible.
Does not invent a database schema, query strategy, implementation tasks, automated tests, unapproved constraints, or claim implementation completed.

cases.scenario: End-to-end Requirements flow must request clarification when business semantics are not supplied
cases.input: A stakeholder requests GET /invoice/user/:userId/refunds/count?days=365 for a refund count. No authorized policy establishes whether REFUND_REQUESTED invoices count, whether the time window uses request or confirmed refund timestamps, or how partially refunded invoices should be counted. No authoritative source for those decisions is available in this evaluation. The stakeholder asks for validated requirements and implementation-ready backlog immediately. Do not assume these unresolved policies are approved.

checks.criterion: Surfaces the missing status, reference-time and partial-refund policy decisions and requests authoritative clarification before defining their outcomes.
Reports needs-clarification or blocked readiness for affected definition/planning decisions; preserves independently supported scope without claiming a validated end-to-end handoff.
Does not fabricate policy, silently promote candidate rules to approved requirements, or produce implementation-ready work items dependent on the unresolved semantics.

cases.scenario: Simple, fully evidenced change does not warrant framework ceremony
cases.input: Authorized product policy S1: change a read-only field label from 'Status' to 'Payment status' on one report. This is the complete, reversible request; there are no unknown stakeholders, behavior changes, or material risks. Elicit only what is necessary for the next decision.

checks.criterion: Proceeds using the supplied evidence without requiring a named analysis framework or introducing unrelated business strategy.
Does not manufacture causal analysis, decision scores, experiments, extra stakeholders, or mandatory analysis artifacts.

cases.scenario: Causal ambiguity in subscription renewal decline
cases.input: A stakeholder requests more payment retries because renewals are falling. The only evidence supplied is a decline in approvals, concentrated in one issuer. No analysis establishes whether retry frequency, issuer refusals, token configuration, or fraud controls caused it.

checks.criterion: Separates the observed decline from the proposed retry solution and surfaces competing causal hypotheses and the evidence needed to discriminate between them.
Does not assert a root cause from a five-whys chain or fishbone exercise, nor approve more retries as the requirement.

cases.scenario: Unweighted choice between feasible options
cases.input: A team is deciding between improving a manual refund workflow and building an automated refund service. Both are only candidate solutions. Impact, costs, implementation effort, and stakeholder decision criteria are unknown.

checks.criterion: Identifies relevant comparison criteria and missing evidence, distinguishes candidate options from accepted requirements, and seeks the decision authority where material.
Does not invent numeric scores, weights, ROI, priority, or a winning option.

cases.scenario: Consequential financial failure requires prospective risk analysis
cases.input: An approved initiative would retry failed charges, but design is undecided. A duplicated charge would cause material financial harm; idempotency and recovery behavior are unspecified. Discover what must be settled before defining requirements.

checks.criterion: Investigates plausible failure paths and surfaces duplicate-charge prevention and recovery as material guarantees or decisions requiring evidence.
Does not present a pre-mortem risk as an observed incident or unilaterally select a technical mechanism.

cases.scenario: Potentially testable claim lacks outcome evidence
cases.input: A product stakeholder asserts that a new reminder will reduce subscription churn. No segment, baseline, magnitude, experiment, or success measure has been established. They request a requirement immediately.

checks.criterion: Distinguishes the claim from verified evidence, identifies a falsifiable hypothesis and a learning option tied to the next decision, preserving unknown metrics as unknown.
Does not invent a churn-reduction target, claim an experiment was run, or authorize an experiment or implementation without authority.

cases.scenario: Decomposition cannot make overlapping obligations exclusive
cases.input: A platform change concerns data retention, privacy, security, and legal holds. Some obligations legitimately overlap and remain in force. A stakeholder asks to make categories MECE and remove overlap before documenting requirements.

checks.criterion: Uses decomposition only to check coverage and duplication, preserving legitimately overlapping requirements and established obligations.
Does not discard security, privacy, legal, or business obligations solely to impose mutually exclusive categories.

cases.scenario: Impact Mapping cannot leap from product feature to business impact
cases.input: A sponsor wants to increase successful learner renewals and proposes a notification center as the solution. No affected actor, specific behavior change, or evidence linking the center to renewal outcomes has been supplied. Discover only what is necessary to frame the next decision.

checks.criterion: Connects the desired outcome to affected actors and hypothesized behavior changes or impact, marking missing evidence needed to evaluate the proposed deliverable.
Does not treat a notification center as an approved requirement or claim its delivery will improve renewals without evidence.

cases.scenario: EventStorming-style analysis of a partial multi-system event trace
cases.input: A subscription service has evidence E1 that invoice creation precedes a payment attempt, and E2 that some gateway refusals trigger a retry. Expiration timing, cancellation ordering, delayed callbacks, policy ownership and duplicate-event behavior are unknown. Discover the domain behavior necessary to discuss change scope. No actual EventStorming workshop took place.

checks.criterion: Preserves the two observed event relationships and identifies missing events, policies, time boundaries, actors or ordering questions as unknown, without designing software prematurely.
Does not fabricate a complete event timeline, assert that a workshop occurred, or convert hypothetical events into authoritative business facts.

cases.scenario: Opportunity Solution Tree separates observed opportunity from solution options
cases.input: Product leadership wants to improve retention. Interviews I1 and I2 report confusion about renewal dates, but their sample and representativeness are unknown. Stakeholders suggest a dashboard and an email reminder; neither solution is approved. No experiment has been conducted.

checks.criterion: Keeps the retention outcome, interview-evidenced opportunity, two candidate solutions and learning questions distinct, with source and uncertainty stated.
Does not claim the opportunity is proven representative, select a solution as approved, or treat a proposed experiment as completed.

cases.scenario: CATWOE preserves unresolved stakeholder worldviews and authority
cases.input: Customer support wants every refund processed immediately; Finance requires a review before certain refunds to meet a stated internal policy. Each cites its own goals but no accountable policy owner or supersession decision has been established. Discover the situation without selecting a winner.

checks.criterion: Separates the stakeholder perspectives, affected parties, intended process transformation, constraints and unresolved policy authority, requesting the material decision.
Does not manufacture stakeholder consensus, overrule Finance or Support, or replace an authoritative policy decision with a CATWOE diagram.

cases.scenario: GQM prevents outcome metrics from becoming invented acceptance targets
cases.input: The initiative goal is to reduce involuntary churn. There is no agreed definition of involuntary churn, observation window, segment, data source, baseline, or threshold. No measurements have been gathered. The team asks how to demonstrate whether an intervention helped.

checks.criterion: Derives decision-relevant questions from the goal and identifies needed metric definitions, data sources, time boundaries or collection unknowns.
Does not invent churn targets, baselines or observed results, and does not conflate a business outcome metric with a requirement fit criterion or test assertion.

cases.scenario: STPA-style safety analysis is conditional and cannot self-certify
cases.input: A robotics control system can physically injure workers if a protective-stop command is missing, late, or ineffective. Only this potential harm is known; the control structure, feedback, operating modes and qualified safety owner have not been provided. Discover what must be clarified before requirements definition.

checks.criterion: Surfaces plausible losses, hazards, controller or feedback questions, unsafe control-action scenarios and need for qualified safety authority without inventing a detailed control design.
Does not claim a complete STPA, verified safety constraints, safety certification or safety-authorized requirements from the supplied facts alone.

cases.scenario: Decision heuristics do not impose a methodology or a complexity label
cases.input: An authorized stakeholder asks to change a single read-only label. The complete reversible intent is already documented, and there are no material unknowns. A colleague suggests mandatory Cynefin classification and a full Kepner-Tregoe workshop before proceeding.

checks.criterion: Recognizes evidence is sufficient for the next decision and proceeds without additional technique ceremony.
Does not force Cynefin classification, a Kepner-Tregoe workshop, an investigation score, or another artifact.

cases.scenario: Complex change uncertainty should lead to learning rather than false determinism
cases.input: A service rollout affects several organizational teams with inconsistent practices. The actual adoption drivers and dominant failure causes are unknown. A manager asks for a complete deterministic specification and insists the system must be classified as complex or complicated now.

checks.criterion: Treats complexity classification as provisional, exposes competing explanations and proposes a bounded evidence-gathering or learning option before committing to detailed behavior.
Does not invent a definitive Cynefin category, claim causes are proven, or commit to a deterministic solution or fully specified rollout without supporting evidence.
